subject: Anthropology
title: Cross-Cultural Comparison
description: Learn Cross-Cultural Comparison in one minute.

hook.text: Marriage exists everywhere. But it looks wildly different — one spouse, four spouses, bride price, dowry.

buildup.text: Cross-cultural comparison examines the same institution or practice across multiple societies to find patterns.

discovery.text: George Murdock's Human Relations Area Files catalog data on hundreds of cultures, enabling large-scale comparison.

twist.text: Comparing cultures risks oversimplifying. Context matters — a ritual in Bali isn't the same as a similar one in Peru.

climax.text: Comparison reveals both human universals and stunning diversity — the twin engines of anthropological insight.

punchline.text: Patterns emerge only when you compare.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of cross-cultural comparison?
options: To rank cultures from best to worst
To find patterns and differences across societies
To prove all cultures are identical

details.summary: Cross-cultural comparison examines similar phenomena across different cultures to identify patterns, test hypotheses, and reveal both human universals and cultural variation. It is anthropology's primary method for generating broadly applicable knowledge from culturally specific observations.
details.whyItMatters: Without comparison, anthropology would be a collection of isolated case studies. Cross-cultural comparison reveals both the range of human possibility and the recurring patterns that suggest underlying constraints on how societies can be organized.
takeaways: Comparison examines phenomena across different cultural contexts
It identifies universal patterns and culturally specific variations
It transforms case studies into broadly applicable knowledge

faq.question: What are the dangers of cross-cultural comparison?
faq.answer: Comparing phenomena out of context can produce misleading similarities. Concepts that seem equivalent across cultures may have fundamentally different meanings locally. The comparative method works best when combined with deep contextual understanding of each case being compared.

faq.question: What databases support cross-cultural comparison?
faq.answer: The Human Relations Area Files and the Ethnographic Atlas compile ethnographic data from hundreds of cultures in standardized formats. These databases enable statistical cross-cultural analysis, though critics note they flatten cultural complexity into coded categories.
